title: Account Solution Architect
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com . What You’ll Do: The infrastructure powering the AI era doesn’t sell itself, and the customers building on it don’t want to be sold to. They want a peer. You’ll work as part of a focused three-person team alongside one Account Executive and one Account Manager, together responsible for landing new accounts and expanding within them across the region. The customers you’ll work with are AI labs, research institutions, and enterprises running some of the most demanding GPU workloads in the world. This is a role for someone who shows up with substance, who can hold a real conversation about model training and MLOps tooling in the morning and cluster networking in the afternoon, and who finds the space between infrastructure and application more interesting than either on its own. About the Role: As an Account Solution Architect covering Northern EMEA, you’ll move across the full stack depending on what the customer needs, from ML training workflows and MLOps platforms like Weights & Biases to bare metal GPU infrastructure and physical AI deployments. This isn’t a role built around a single layer of the stack, but the majority of your conversations will live in the ML layer. You’ll be expected to go deeper than most when the infrastructure conversation demands it, while staying commercially aware enough to support both new logo pursuits and in-flight account expansion. This role requires up to 40% travel. In this role, you will: Cover Northern EMEA, with a focus on the Nordics and Benelux regions (Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg). Work closely with one Account Executive and one Account Manager as a dedicated three-person unit, supporting the full land and expand motion across the region. Lead technical discovery with prospects and existing customers to understand model training requirements, MLOps workflows, and infrastructure constraints. Design and present solutions spanning ML infrastructure, GPU compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes-based orchestration, and MLOps tooling. Run proof-of-concept engagements and architecture reviews, and see them through to a decision. Act as the internal voice of the customer, feeding technical requirements and product gaps back to Engineering and Product. Maintain clear documentation of customer architectures, solution designs, and outstanding technical questions. Who You Are: 3+ years in a pre-sales, solutions engineering, or solutions architecture role, ideally with a focus on AI/ML platforms, cloud infrastructure, or HPC. Strong working knowledge of ML training and inference workflows - you understand how models are built, optimized, and deployed, not just where they run. Hands-on familiarity with MLOps platforms and the tooling AI teams use day-to-day, including experiment tracking, pipeline orchestration, and model serving. Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX. Comfortable going below the SaaS layer when the conversation demands it - GPU topology, network fabric, and cluster architecture shouldn’t be unfamiliar territory. Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containerized workloads at scale. Strong communication skills - you can adjust your register from a research engineer to a VP of Infrastructure without losing credibility at either end. Experience managing multiple concurrent opportunities across a geographic territory. Fluency in English required; proficiency in Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, or Finnish is a plus. Preferred: Familiarity with NVIDIA GPU architectures (H100, A100, H200) and the software stack around them: CUDA, NCCL, cuDNN. Working knowledge of high-performance networking concepts: InfiniBand, RDMA, RoCE, TCP/IP. Background working directly with AI labs, research institutions, or enterprise ML teams. Exposure to physical AI use cases and the infrastructure requirements they bring. Experience with Salesforce, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools. Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams - even if you aren’t a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk. You’re comfortable going one layer deeper than the demo - whether that’s a networking topology, a training job that won’t converge, or a rack layout question from a facilities team. You’ve worked across more than one layer of the stack and find the intersections more interesting than any single discipline. You thrive in a fast-moving environment and take ownership of your region like it’s your own business. You’re a natural collaborator who makes the people around you - including your AE and AM - better at their jobs. Why CoreWeave? At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values: Be Curious at Your Core Act Like an Owner Empower Employees Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences Achieve More Together We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us! The starting salary will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility). #LIjobs What We Offer The range we’ve posted represents the typical compensation range for this role. To determine actual compensation, we review the market rate for each candidate which can include a variety of factors. These include qualifications, experience, interview performance, and location. In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings for full-time employees; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include: Medical, dental, and vision insurance - 100% paid for by CoreWeave Company-paid Life Insurance Voluntary supplemental life insurance Short and long-term disability insurance Flexible Spending Account Health Savings Account Tuition Reimbursement Ability to Participate in Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP) Mental Wellness Benefits through Spring Health Family-Forming support provided by Carrot Paid Parental Leave Flexible, full-service childcare support with Kinside 401(k) with a generous employer match Flexible PTO Catered lunch each day in our office and data center locations A casual work environment A work culture focused on innovative disruption California Applicants California Consumer Privacy Act Equal Opportunity & Accommodations CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace

title: Senior Talent Acquisition Manager – Commercial (f/m/d)
description: About Cosuno Construction is a €14 trillion industry that still runs on email, spreadsheets and scanned PDFs. Cosuno is replacing that with AI. General contractors tender their projects on our platform to more than 250,000 subcontractors, and our agentic AI matches the right firms, flags anomalies in bids and benchmarks every price against 6.5 million data points from over €136 billion in processed bid volume. Every tender makes the AI smarter. The results are measurable: general contractors cut costs by around 6 %, subcontractors win 22 % more volume, and every new general contractor customer this year has chosen our AI product. Founded in Berlin in 2019 and backed by Cherry Ventures and Spark Capital with over €40 million raised, we are now scaling Sales, Customer Success and Marketing with that capital. That is where you come in. Your mission As our Senior Talent Acquisition Manager – Commercial, you make sure every seat in Sales, Customer Success and Marketing goes to someone exceptional. You report to Fritz Cramer, Co-CEO, and work closely with our VP Sales, Head of SC Sales, Head of Customer Success and Marketing Lead. That means real ownership: you shape how Cosuno hires, not just who . What you will achieve in your first 12 months You hire 25 people across Account Executives, Customer Success and Inside Sales Managers, owning every process from intake to signed contract. You build warm pipelines before roles open, so we hire through sourcing and referrals instead of agencies. You turn every role into a clear scorecard and give hiring managers structured interviews they actually use. You relaunch our referral programme and turn our team into our best talent scouts. You make hiring measurable with a monthly dashboard on time-to-hire, conversion and source of hire. What the job really looks like A large part of your week is active sourcing and candidate conversations. If you prefer managing agencies, this role is not for you. You run several commercial processes in parallel, with ambitious hiring managers who want great people fast. There is no large TA team and no finished playbook. You build the processes while you hire. You push back when a profile or a decision is not right. We want you to. What you bring At least 4 years of recruiting experience, of which at least 2 years in-house at a high-growth B2B SaaS company, hiring SDRs and Account Executives. A track record you can prove in numbers: hires made, time-to-hire and offer acceptance rate. You steer your pipeline by data, not gut feeling. Proven sourcing skills: you have filled roles through direct outreach and can show what worked. Structured assessment: you run scorecard-based interviews and can tell real sales talent from a good pitch. Strong closing skills: you win top candidates against competing offers and counteroffers. Strong stakeholder management: you advise hiring managers and challenge them when it matters. Fluent German and English, written and spoken. Nice to have Hands-on experience with Ashby, LinkedIn Recruiter, Clay or Lusha. You use AI tools and automation in sourcing and outreach. Curiosity about construction or other traditional industries. What we offer Salary: €70,000–90,000 gross base salary per year, depending on experience, plus a variable component of 25 % of your base salary at 100 % target achievement, tied to hires who successfully complete their probation period. AI at the core: you work with Ashby, LinkedIn Recruiter, Clay and Lusha, and you have a budget to test new tools. Learning budget for your professional development. Time off: 25-30 vacation days per year. Flexibility: fully remote within Germany or from our office in Berlin-Kreuzberg, with flexible hours. A great team: open and international, with regular off-sites and team events. Stability: permanent contract in a well-funded company. Our hiring process (max. 3 weeks) Intro call with Vivien (People Lead), 30 minutes, video. Career deep-dive with Fritz (Co-CEO) 30 minutes, video. Live case study: together with two of our hiring managers (Basti, Kornelius or Caspar), you work through a sourcing case for a fictional SDR role, 60 minutes, preferably in our Berlin office. References: with your consent only, we speak with 2–3 hiring managers you have recruited for in previous roles. Offer. From your first call to our decision, the process takes no longer than 3 weeks. Your contact: Vivien Littmann, People Lead We welcome applications from everyone who brings the skills for this role, regardless of background or circumstances. If you need any adjustments during the process, just let us know. title: Research Scientist, Protein Design & Engineering
description: About us We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient. If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it. We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK. The role You'll engineer proteins to carry out useful chemistry, combining enzyme discovery, directed evolution, and experimental characterisation. You'll own the experimental cycle: choosing starting points, building variant libraries, developing screens, and establishing which changes improve function and why. This is a hands-on role working closely with our computational and ML teams. You'll test designed proteins at the bench, use experimental results to guide subsequent rounds, and develop enzymes with the activity, selectivity, and stability needed for their intended application. There’s no fixed screening pipeline to inherit — you'll help decide how we build it. What you'll do Design and run protein engineering campaigns, from initial enzyme selection and library design through screening and characterisation of improved variants. Build and express variant libraries using site-directed, random, and combinatorial mutagenesis. Develop assays and high-throughput screens that reliably measure the properties we're trying to improve. Express, purify, and characterise proteins, measuring kinetics, substrate scope, selectivity, and stability under relevant reaction conditions. Work with computational scientists to test proposed designs, interpret successes and failures, and use the results to guide the next round. Develop enzymatic reactions and cascades, identifying how enzyme performance, cofactors, and reaction conditions affect overall productivity. Essential experience We're interested in the engineering campaigns you've run, the assays you've built, and what you learned from them. We care about: A track record of improving protein or enzyme function through directed evolution or rational engineering. Practical fluency in molecular biology, including cloning, library construction, mutagenesis, and recombinant protein expression. Experience developing and troubleshooting enzyme assays and screening workflows, with appropriate controls and follow-up validation. A solid grasp of enzyme mechanism, kinetics, and structure–function relationships, and the ability to use these to guide experiments. Experience independently taking projects through multiple design–build–test cycles and explaining what drove the results. Highly preferred Experience with industrial biocatalysis or engineering enzymes for demanding reaction conditions. Experience integrating liquid handling and laboratory automation with high-throughput screening. Familiarity with biosensor-based screens, growth-based selection, or FACS. Experience testing computationally designed proteins and feeding experimental results back into design. Experience with enzyme cascades, fermentation, or transferring enzymatic processes from the bench to larger scales. Logistics This is a full-time, on-site role in Cambridge, MA. About the role: As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission. This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. Your responsibilities will include: Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar You're a great fit if you: Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code. The team owns the full model serving stack — from GPU-resident inference runtimes and deployment infrastructure through to the developer platform that enables every other research team to bring their models to production. The broader Research organisation publishes regularly at ACL, NeurIPS, and EMNLP, and the Production Inference team brings that same culture of rigour and innovation to the systems layer of AI. While this is not a hands-on coding role, you will be deeply involved in technical reviews, architecture decisions, and research direction for the inference stack. Operate with a high degree of autonomy, defining the team's direction and pushing for results in an environment where requirements from product or commercial stakeholders can be ambiguous or evolving. Play an active role in identifying, assessing, and recruiting research and engineering talent as the team continues to develop. You are comfortable operating across the full model lifecycle — from training handoff through to production deployment, monitoring, and efficiency improvement — and understand infrastructure and compute constraints without needing to own them directly. You have excellent communication skills and the ability to translate complex technical direction into clear goals for both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You are solution-oriented and decisive, able to define direction and drive outcomes without waiting for direction from above. With flexible working hours and trust in your productivity, we are in sync with your team’s general locations and time zones to foster effective and seamless collaboration. Regular in-person team events : we bond over vibrant events that are as unique as our team, from local team and business unit gatherings, to new-joiner onboardings, to company-wide events that bring us all together–literally. Monthly full-day hacking sessions : every month, we have Hack Fridays, where you can spend your time diving into a project you're passionate about and get the opportunity to work with other teams–we value your initiatives, impact, and creativity. 30 days of annual leave : we value your peace of mind. title: System Architect
description: Are you an experienced System Architect with a passion for intelligent building management systems, industrial automation, and safety-critical applications? At Deerns, you will have the opportunity to work on innovative and challenging projects that contribute to a smarter, safer, and more sustainable future. Read on and discover how you can make an impact. The challenge The System Architect for Intelligent Building Management Solutions and Industrial Automation plays a crucial role in designing integrated automation solutions for both buildings and industrial processes. This position involves developing safe, efficient, and future-ready systems that connect various installations, such as HVAC, lighting, access control, gas safety, and industrial process control. You will work closely with project teams, suppliers, and end-users to create innovative and sustainable solutions that meet the highest safety standards. Your responsibilities include: Developing automation architectures: Design scalable solutions for intelligent building management and process automation, including gas detection systems, safety mechanisms, and process control. System integration: Connect installations using protocols like BACnet, Modbus, KNX, and industrial standards such as OPC UA and PROFIBUS. Gas safety and process safety: Develop solutions for gas detection, emergency shutdowns, ventilation integration, and fail-safe control systems for industrial environments. Specification and standards management: Implement relevant standards for intelligent building management solutions, process automation, and safety systems, such as IEC 61511 (functional safety) and ATEX regulations. Process optimization: Analyze and optimize industrial processes and systems to enhance efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Stakeholder management: Collaborate effectively with various stakeholders, including clients, end-users, engineers, and project managers, ensuring solutions meet both functional and technical requirements. Continuous learning and development: Stay updated on the latest innovations in smart technologies and automation, applying these to develop improved, future-proof solutions. • Technological consulting: Identify innovations to enhance performance and reliability in intelligent buildings and industrial environments. Documentation and communication: Prepare technical documentation and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders. Required Skills and Competencies: Extensive knowledge of intelligent building management solutions, gas safety systems, and industrial process control. Expertise in communication standards and protocols such as KNX, BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, and PROFIBUS. Proficiency in designing fail-safe systems and safety-critical applications. Experience with IT networks and cybersecurity in automation environments. Strong analytical skills and problem-solving abilities. Flexibility and the ability to continuously adapt to technological advancements. Excellent communication skills to clearly present complex technical issues Education and Experience: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation Technology, or a related field. Relevant experience in intelligent building management solutions, industrial automation, and safety-critical systems. This role combines technological innovation with safety-critical applications. As a System Architect, you will develop integrated solutions that maximize comfort, safety, efficiency, and sustainability in both buildings and industrial processes. We offer A position of 32-40 hours per week with a salary to match. Challenging projects for leading clients in the Netherlands and internationally. A work environment in which innovation and sustainability are put into practice daily. Attention to your own development and vitality with ample training and development opportunities, bicycle and sports arrangements, flexible working hours, 33 vacation days and the possibility of purchasing additional days. Hybrid working, where you have the opportunity to alternate between working from home and the office. A team where cooperation and collegiality are priority, and where we interact informally. Sustainability is in our genes. This is expressed, for example, in a mobility policy where health and sustainability are most important. Many of our offices are located near public transport hubs, cycling is encouraged, and your travel expenses are reimbursed 100% on the basis of public transport. About Deerns As an independent engineering firm, Deerns specializes in consultancy, design and implementation supervision in the fields of installation engineering, building physics, energy supply and sustainability. Our areas of expertise contribute to sustainable, intelligent and future-proof buildings that optimally support our clients' processes. We are responsible for designing the installations and realizing good comfort and a pleasant climate in a wide variety of buildings; from offices, to airports and from hospitals to data centers. description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat. DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt now operate as one global company. Behind the AI experiences millions of people use every day, from shopping assistants to customer support agents, sits one shared Generative AI platform. Our team builds it. We're looking for a Staff Product Manager in London to own major parts of that platform. Your customers are the engineers and ML researchers across all three brands who build AI products and agents. You'll work with engineering and product leaders in Europe and the US, and your decisions will shape how AI gets built across every market we operate in. What You'll Be Doing Set the strategy and roadmap for core parts of our GenAI platform: model access and routing, agent infrastructure, and evaluation and observability. Build one platform for three brands. Spot the patterns across Deliveroo, Wolt and DoorDash teams and turn them into shared building blocks, so a capability built once reaches every market. Shape our model portfolio across frontier and open-weight models. Decide where we build, buy or partner in an ecosystem that changes month to month. Make agents production-ready. Give teams safe access to company knowledge, tools and systems, with the quality, latency and cost controls needed to run agents at scale. Own the evaluation strategy so teams can prove quality before launch and keep improving it after. Stay close to your customers. Work with the teams shipping AI experiences, measure adoption and time-to-production, and let real production use drive the roadmap. Lead at a senior level, presenting to senior technical leadership and influence strategy beyond your own roadmap. What You'll Need to Thrive Our ideal candidate brings deep expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others: Significant product management experience (typically 8+ years, or equivalent), including owning a technical platform, developer product, or ML or data infrastructure. Hands-on experience with LLM-based products or platforms in production, such as assistants, agents, evaluation or inference. GenAI platforms are a young field, so we care more about depth than years. A platform mindset. You notice the problem five teams keep solving and turn it into one capability everyone can use. The ability to go deep with engineers and ML researchers, then explain the trade-off in plain language to a senior leader. A track record of leading large, ambiguous areas on your own and aligning stakeholders across companies, countries and time zones. Comfort with regular overlap with US time zones, including some late-afternoon and evening calls. title: Hoofdmonteur Warmtepompen
description: Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We ontwerpen onze producten zelf, assembleren ze in Utrecht en zorgen samen met onze installatiepartners dat ze bij steeds meer mensen thuis komen te staan. We groeien hard. Tot nu toe worden al onze warmtepompen geïnstalleerd door externe partners, maar daar komt verandering in. We gaan onze eigen installatieteams opbouwen en zoeken daarom een Hoofdmonteur Warmtepompen die hierin het voortouw neemt. Je bent een ervaren monteur die graag zelf de handen uit de mouwen steekt, maar ook energie krijgt van het begeleiden van anderen. Je gaat samen met je team op pad, bent verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit van de installaties en helpt ons om steeds meer monteurs op te leiden. Je komt dus niet in een bestaand team terecht. Je helpt het team zelf opbouwen. Wat ga je doen? Als Hoofdmonteur ben je verantwoordelijk voor de installatie van onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis. Je begint met het leiden van ons eerste interne installatieteam en helpt ons om de komende jaren onze eigen installatiecapaciteit verder uit te bouwen. Je installeert warmtepompen en leidt je team Je gaat samen met een collega-monteur op pad om onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis te installeren. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de volledige installatie, van de technische uitvoering en het oplossen van onverwachte problemen tot de oplevering. Je zorgt dat installaties veilig, efficiënt en volgens onze kwaliteitsstandaarden worden uitgevoerd. Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor de klant tijdens de installatie. Je legt uit wat jullie doen, beantwoordt vragen en zorgt dat de klant met een goed gevoel achterblijft. Je stemt waar nodig af met onze werkvoorbereiders en collega's op kantoor over planning, materialen en technische uitdagingen. Je bouwt mee aan ons interne installatieteam Je begeleidt en traint nieuwe monteurs en helpt hen om zelfstandig installaties uit te kunnen voeren. Je denkt mee over het aannemen van nieuwe collega's en hoe we ons installatieteam verder kunnen uitbreiden. Je helpt onze installatiestandaarden en werkwijzen verder te ontwikkelen. Je signaleert wat er in de praktijk beter of slimmer kan en neemt initiatief om dit te verbeteren. Je deelt feedback vanuit het veld met onze engineers, werkvoorbereiders en productontwikkelaars, zodat we onze producten en installaties continu kunnen verbeteren. Wie zoeken wij? We zoeken iemand die zijn vak goed verstaat, verantwoordelijkheid neemt en het leuk vindt om anderen beter te maken. Je hoeft niet eerder een heel team te hebben opgebouwd, maar je moet wel zin hebben om die uitdaging aan te gaan. Je hebt ruime ervaring met het installeren van warmtepompen, cv-installaties of andere verwarmingssystemen. Ervaring met warmtepompen heeft een sterke voorkeur. Je hebt een goede technische basis in installatietechniek, elektrotechniek en/of werktuigbouwkunde. Je kunt zelfstandig installaties uitvoeren, technische tekeningen lezen en onverwachte problemen oplossen. Je hebt ervaring met het begeleiden van andere monteurs, of bent klaar om die verantwoordelijkheid op je te nemen. Je werkt nauwkeurig en veilig en vindt het belangrijk om goed werk af te leveren. Je communiceert makkelijk met klanten en collega's en kunt technische zaken begrijpelijk uitleggen. Je neemt initiatief, denkt in oplossingen en voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het eindresultaat. Je spreekt goed Nederlands en hebt rijbewijs B. Een relevante mbo-opleiding en certificeringen zoals VCA, NEN 3140 of CO-vakmanschap zijn mooi meegenomen. Heb je nog niet alle benodigde certificaten? Dan kijken we samen wat je nog kunt behalen. Wat bieden wij jou? Een salaris van €4.000 tot €6.000 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur, afhankelijk van je ervaring. Een sleutelrol in ons bedrijf: je wordt de eerste Hoofdmonteur van ons interne installatieteam en helpt dit verder uit te bouwen. Veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid: je krijgt de ruimte om mee te denken over hoe we installeren, samenwerken en nieuwe monteurs opleiden. Goed materiaal: een volledig uitgeruste werkbus en professioneel gereedschap. 26 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV-dagen op basis van 40 uur, met de mogelijkheid om te kiezen voor een hogere beloning in plaats van ADV. Een goede pensioenregeling volgens de cao Metaal & Techniek. Mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen, zowel technisch als in het begeleiden en aansturen van een team. Een betrokken team met korte lijnen, weinig bureaucratie en regelmatig leuke activiteiten, van borrels en teamuitjes tot onze jaarlijkse wintersport. Waarom DeWarmte? Bij DeWarmte geloven we dat verduurzaming pas echt werkt als het voor iedereen bereikbaar en aantrekkelijk is. Daarom ontwikkelen we slimme, betaalbare warmtepompen die we zelf ontwerpen en assembleren. We zijn een groeiend bedrijf waar veel gebeurt en waar je echt invloed hebt op hoe we dingen aanpakken. We houden van mensen die initiatief nemen, samenwerken en niet wachten tot iemand anders een probleem oplost. Als Hoofdmonteur krijg je de kans om vanaf het begin mee te bouwen aan onze eigen installatieorganisatie. Je werkt zelf aan mooie technische installaties, leidt nieuwe monteurs op en helpt bepalen hoe we dit in de toekomst op grotere schaal gaan doen. Klaar om samen met ons iets op te bouwen? Solliciteer en kom kennismaken. We vertellen je graag meer over DeWarmte, onze warmtepompen en onze plannen voor het interne installatieteam. Compensation: €4K – €6K per month • €4K – €6K per month Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Flight Test Instrumentation & Data Engineer
description: The Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & Data Engineer will be responsible for the end-to-end handling, quality assurance, accessibility, and long-term management of all flight data. The primary objective is to ensure that full-aircraft data, from the onboard sensors and DAQ systems to the final processing tools, is available to every engineering team through a reliable, efficient, and standardized workflow. Tasks Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & DAQ Pipeline Manage the data pipeline from the physical sensor and Data Acquisition (DAQ) level for the full aircraft, ensuring seamless and accurate transmission into the telemetry and storage systems. Maintain sensor configuration, calibration records, and metadata to guarantee the accurate translation of raw physical signals into usable engineering units. Collaborate with hardware, software and integration teams to define sensor requirements, DAQ architectures, scaling, and telemetry bandwidth allocations. Troubleshoot and resolve data anomalies at the DAQ and sensor level (e.g., signal noise, dropouts, faulty scaling) before they propagate into downstream databases. Data Infrastructure & Accessibility Maintain reliable extraction of flight data from InfluxDB. Develop and maintain standardized local data structures for analysis, plotting, and visualization. Optimize access to large flight datasets while minimizing CPU and memory usage. Design and maintain an efficient local storage solution for processed flight data. Support future improvements to the flight data architecture as storage requirements, sensor counts, and analysis needs continue to evolve. Data Quality & Analysis Support Maintain derived datasets to ensure common calculations and signals are shared consistently across teams. Ensure strict timing synchronization and timestamp accuracy across all recorded data, from the sensor acquisition point to the database. Monitor data quality, completeness, and integrity throughout the entire pipeline. Provide fast data previews for rapid post-flight reviews. Enable efficient access to high-frequency sensor data for detailed engineering investigations. Support custom querying of processed datasets. Requirements Education & Experience Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related technical field. 3+ years of professional experience in test instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ), or sensor-to-database time-series data engineering (aerospace, automotive, or racing/motorsports preferred). Hands-on experience working directly with physical aircraft/vehicle sensor installations, DAQ hardware, and telemetry pipelines. Technical & Domain Expertise 1. Hardware, Sensors & DAQ Architecture Strong understanding of physical sensors (e.g., strain gauges, accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, RTDs, LVDTs, pitot-static tubes). Demonstrated knowledge of signal conditioning, sampling rate selection, anti-aliasing filtering, scaling, and sensor calibration procedures. 2. Data Infrastructure & Software Development Proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automated data processing, and visualization library development (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, SciPy). Experience working with time-series databases, specifically InfluxDB (or similar engines), including writing efficient queries (Flux/InfluxQL) and data retrieval pipelines. Solid foundation in data structures and memory/CPU optimization when handling high-memory high-frequency continuous time-series datasets. 3. Data Integrity & Signal Processing Experience with timestamping and clock synchronization protocols across distributed DAQ hardware and storage nodes. Knowledge of basic digital signal processing (DSP) concepts (filtering, FFT, spectral analysis, decimation/resampling). Soft Skills & Work Style Cross-functional communication: Ability to bridge the gap between hardware technicians, flight physics/aerodynamics engineers, and software teams. Detail-oriented mindset: Uncompromising rigor regarding calibration metadata, unit conversions, and data accuracy. Adaptability: Drive to continuously improve data infrastructure as aircraft sensor counts, test frequencies, and analytical needs expand. Preferred / Bonus Qualifications Knowledge of standard FAA / EASA flight test instrumentation requirements or military flight test standards (e.g. IRIG 106). Familiarity with dashboarding tools (e.g., Grafana) for rapid post-flight previews and real-time telemetry display. Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines for internal engineering tool distribution. Direct experience with DAQ systems and digital bus protocols (CAN bus, ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, Ethernet/UDP, PCM). Familiarity with binary flight data formats (e.g., IRIG 106 Chapter 10/11, MDF/MF4, HDF5, Parquet, or custom binary loggers). Experience with performing on-aircraft hardware troubleshooting (e.g., tracking down ground loops, signal noise, dropouts, or faulty scaling). Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

Analyseren van risico’s en helpen bij het opstellen van veiligheidsplannen. Actief meedoen aan toolbox meetings en veiligheidstrainingen. Assisteren bij incidentonderzoeken en meewerken aan verbeterplannen. Ondersteunen bij het implementeren van veiligheidsmaatregelen en -systemen. Dit is jouw team Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Amsterdam is een ontwikkelende bouwer met zo'n 220 enthousiaste collega’s. Onze ambitie is groot en met veel enthousiasme ontwikkelen en bouwen we gezonde en fijne leefomgevingen, waar mensen zich thuis voelen. Benieuwd waar wij ons mee bezig houden? Neem dan eens een kijkje op onze website. Dit bieden wij jou Een stagevergoeding van €700 per maand op basis van 40 uren per week; Je krijgt ruimte voor eigen initiatieven; Tijd voor je schoolopdrachten/examens; De beste collega’s om het vak van te leren en zij zorgen voor een ongekende goede werksfeer; Een familiebedrijf waarin we voor elkaar klaarstaan! title: People & Workplace Experience Manager
description: About Dust Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026. Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 . The role Dust is growing fast, and we want every person who joins us to feel welcome, supported, connected and able to do their best work. As our People Experience Manager, you'll shape how people experience Dust, from their first day and the moments that bring us together to the way our offices in Paris, London, New York and San Francisco support the team. We're looking for someone who is operationally excellent and creatively ambitious. You'll handle the details carefully, and you'll also look for ways to make the employee experience much better. One day you might be redesigning part of onboarding, the next planning a company offsite, acting on survey feedback, or working with a site lead to improve one of our offices. This role works as a partner across the company. You'll work most closely with People Operations, who lead on the core people processes. Together, you'll make sure the employee experience is well run behind the scenes and thoughtful in how people actually experience it. In Paris, you'll also work closely with our Office Manager, who runs our HQ on site and leads much of our day-to-day office life and events. In London, New York and San Francisco, you'll coordinate with local site leads. You'll also work with IT, Finance, Legal, Marketing, leadership and outside partners. Your guiding principle: consistency where it matters, local adaptation where it creates a better experience. What you will do: Own the employee journey Own the onboarding experience end to end, working closely with our People Ops Specialist, from pre-boarding and equipment to first-day logistics and the first few weeks, so new joiners can contribute from day one in every location. Work with People Ops, IT, Finance, hiring managers, our Paris Office Manager and site leads so every handoff in the employee journey is smooth. Partner with People Ops and IT on offboarding, so people leave with the same care they got when they joined. Be a trusted point of contact for everyday employee questions and needs, and know when to bring in People Ops. Build culture and community Run and improve our team rituals, including weekly lunches, team drinks, dinners and company gatherings. Organise one or two company offsites or retreats each year. Create moments that help people connect, celebrate progress and feel they belong, across offices and time zones. Pay attention to the details that make experiences feel personal and inclusive, such as dietary needs, accessibility, preferences and team milestones. Partner with People and Marketing on selected external and brand-building events. Listen and turn feedback into action Build feedback loops (surveys, conversations, informal check-ins) to understand how people experience Dust. Turn what people tell us into concrete recommendations and visible improvements. Define and track simple, useful measures of employee and workplace experience. Communicate clearly and consistently about updates, events, practical information and team norms. Be assertive when needed. Shape our workplaces Make sure our offices are safe, welcoming, functional and ergonomic, and that they reflect how we want people to feel at Dust. Work with our office manager on day-to-day operations: supplies, maintenance, access, equipment and services. Manage workplace vendors, contracts and budget, and look for efficient ways to improve the experience. Spot operational needs early and fix issues before they disrupt anyone. Scale the experience as Dust grows Help shape how our physical, hybrid and digital environments evolve as the company grows. Set up simple, scalable processes and clear ownership across People, IT, Finance and Legal topics. Keep the employee experience personal and high quality without making it bureaucratic. What success looks like After your first 100 days, you will have: Built a smooth, consistent onboarding experience for every new joiner, in every location. Delivered team rituals, events and offsites that strengthen connection and culture. Set up feedback loops and a practical set of metrics that guide People Experience decisions. Created well-run, welcoming offices where operational issues are handled quickly and proactively. Established clear processes and ownership across People, workplace, IT, Finance and Legal. Helped Dust grow its employee experience without it becoming bureaucratic or impersonal. What we are looking for 4+ years of experience in People Operations, People Experience, Workplace Experience in a fast growing, globally distributed environment A proactive generalist who can handle many kinds of work at once without losing sight of the bigger picture. Real ideas, sound judgement and the confidence to improve how things work today. Strong operational ownership, project management skills and attention to detail. Warmth, empathy and a genuine interest in helping people feel comfortable and connected. Clear, direct, thoughtful communication, and discretion with sensitive situations. Confidence working with vendors, budgets and outside partners. The ability to build simple processes that scale, and to keep a high bar for quality while staying pragmatic. Comfort with a fast-moving environment where priorities can change, working on your own while collaborating across the company. Location We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together. We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect. That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call. Why Dust The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves. We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk. Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. Learn how we think and work. Our product constitution, a story about our mission Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human , Stanislas Polu , Viva

title: Junior Transformation Strategist (UK Based)
description: About Duvo Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together. Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result. Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail. We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome. Every solution carries a contracted 5x ROI guarantee. The role As a Junior Transformation Strategist, you are the insight and output engine beside our Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts. On bigger engagements we need more than technical delivery. We need someone who can take a messy process, find the critical question, get to a clear insight fast, and put it into materials a customer team will act on. Today that work often lands on Forward Deployed Engineers. That is the wrong use of a scarce technical resource. This role exists so that insight work has a dedicated owner. You will work alongside Transformation Strategists (who own day-to-day account presence and workstream direction) and Forward Deployed Engineers (who own the technical solution). You do not own the executive relationship or the commercial outcome. You own the speed and quality of the analytical and written work that makes those conversations possible. This is a fungible problem-solving role. You will be thrown at different accounts and different problem types (category, supply chain, finance ops, inventory, commercial) and expected to produce. Ideal for someone currently ~2–4 years into a client-facing career as an Associate, Senior Associate, or Consultant at McKinsey or BCG who wants concentrated ownership, not another staffing cycle. We want to hire two people into this role quickly. What you will do 1. Get to the insight Dive into how work actually happens: interviews, extracts, handoffs, exceptions and the workarounds people use to keep things running. Build a fact base that shows where cost, cash, service, cycle time or control is being lost. Form a hypothesis early, name what would kill it, and pressure-test it with the Transformation Strategist before you polish anything. Structure unfamiliar problems without waiting for a perfect brief. Frame the selection equation (what matters, what does not) so the team and the customer can decide. 2. Deliver output that moves a decision Turn analysis into decision-ready slides, one-pagers and memos that make the important choice obvious. Be exact about baselines, assumptions and evidence. Do not use polish to hide uncertainty. Work fast: same-day or next-day turnarounds on defined asks are the norm, not the exception. Produce materials a Transformation Strategist can take into a working session or steerco with minimal rewrite. 3. Be fungible surge capacity on big accounts Plug into multiple live enterprise accounts as extra hands where the Transformation Strategist needs analytical depth. Jump between problem types without needing a long ramp each time. Keep a clean trail of actions, open questions and evidence so work can be handed between you, the Transformation Strategist and the FDE without loss. Surface blockers early; do not sit on ambiguity hoping it resolves. 4. Build the evidence for impact Help lock baseline, target and measurement window before implementation. Quantify results in language a CFO would trust (revenue, margin, cost, working capital, cycle time, control), not activity counts or sentiment. Investigate misses as carefully as wins, and turn both into clear evidence packs the Transformation Strategist can use upstairs. 5. Stay close to the customer team (working level) Own relationships with operators and mid-level owners who live the process day to day. Prepare working sessions, capture decisions and follow commitments through. Know when a question needs a senior call and escalate early rather than bluffing. You will not own commercial negotiations, board-level relationships or technical build. You will own the craft and pace of the insight work that makes those outcomes possible. Skills and capabilities we will assess These are explicit. We will hire against them. Structured problem solving. Hypothesis-driven. You can take an unfamiliar operation apart, find the critical question, write a kill criterion, and give a clear recommendation without hiding behind a framework. Analytical speed and numeracy. Comfortable with messy data and incomplete information. You build analyses that are concise, correct and decision-ready under time pressure. Written and slide craft. Your decks and memos are tight. First page says the answer. Evidence follows. A partner or Transformation Strategist can use your output with light edit, not a rewrite. Insight generation. You do not stop at describing the process. You find where value is lost and what to change first. Fungibility. You can be dropped onto a new account or a new problem type and produce within days, not weeks. Delivery bias. You stay after the framing is done. You follow actions through. You notice what is not working and help fix it. Customer judgment at working level. You listen well, ask a direct question and communicate clearly with operators and managers. You know when to escalate. AI-native personal workflow. You use AI seriously to accelerate research, analysis and drafting, and you remain responsible for the quality of what goes in front of a customer. Early-stage working style. You move without perfect instructions, write in plain English and surface bad news early. Who we are looking for Currently an Associate, Senior Associate or Consultant (or equivalent) at McKinsey or BCG, typically ~2–4 years of core, client-facing consulting experience. Bain and other top strategy firms can fit if the craft is the same. A track record of producing high-quality analyses and slides that partners and clients actually used to decide. Evidence you can work quickly without sacrificing rigor. Comfort operating as surge capacity across problems rather than owning a single long study end to end alone. Helpful but not required: retail, CPG, supply chain, logistics, inventory or finance operations exposure; prior startup or early-stage experience. What good looks like after 12 months Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts treat you as the person they call when they need a sharp fact base, a clean deck or a second pair of eyes on an insight, within hours not days. You have supported multiple accounts and problem types without losing quality. At least one measured process change carries analysis and evidence you built. Your templates, diagnostics and slide patterns are reused by the next Junior Transformation Strategist. FDEs on those accounts spend their time on technical delivery, not insight decks. This role is not for you if You want to own the C-level relationship, commercial negotiation or full transformation roadmap from day one. That is the Transformation Strategist / Senior path. You only enjoy the framing phase and lose interest once the work becomes detailed. You need perfectly clean data, a large analyst team or complete instructions before you can make progress. You see slides as the final product rather than a tool to help a customer decide and act. You want to build automations or live in the technical weeds. That is the Forward Deployed Engineer role. You want a narrow, single-account BA role with little variety or visible accountability. Why leave McKinsey or BCG for this Your insight work lands in live enterprise operations with a contracted 5x ROI, not in a forgo

title: Talent Partner (EU/UK Based - Remote)
description: About the role Duvo helps large enterprises map, optimise and execute the long-running, messy operational work that runs across their systems: ERPs, portals, email, spreadsheets, calls. We sell into Heads of Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and IT at large retailers and FMCG brands. New deals land at €100k–€250k ARR and grow materially through expansion. We're about to grow fast across engineering and go-to-market, and into new European markets, without lowering the bar. Agencies alone can't get us there. We're hiring a Talent Partner who goes out and finds the people themselves, owns a set of roles and EU markets end to end, and works with our hiring managers as a partner, not a scheduling desk. You'll report to Marko, who leads talent at Duvo, and work directly with our founders and hiring managers. What you'll do Own your roles and markets. You'll take a portfolio of roles across engineering and GTM, plus the European markets we're pushing hardest into. Open the role, build the pipeline, run the process, close the offer. You're accountable for the hire landing, not for the funnel looking busy. Source directly. Most of the people we want will never apply. You'll run outbound on LinkedIn and beyond, work referrals properly, and use AI to find candidates nobody else is talking to. When a role opens, you've got people on the phone that week. Own the screen. Every candidate who reaches a hiring manager has been through you first. Strong screening calls, clear written notes, an honest pass or fail. You'd rather reject a maybe than waste a loop. Partner with hiring managers. Agree the bar before the first CV, calibrate in writing, chase feedback until it lands, and push back when a process or a requirement doesn't make sense. Keep the agencies honest. For your markets, brief agency partners properly, hold them to our bar, and cut the ones that send noise. Run a tight, automated process. Scheduling, trial days, logistics, candidate comms. Nothing falls through the cracks, and anything you do twice gets automated. We build AI agents for a living and we run hiring the same way: Ashby underneath, AI across screening, research and interview prep, and agents handling scheduling and chasing. You'll use that system every day and help build the next parts of it. Look after candidates. Everyone who talks to us knows where they stand, quickly, whether it's a yes or a no. Who you are 3+ years in recruiting, in-house at a startup or scale-up or at a tech-focused agency, with full-cycle ownership. A real sourcer. You can show us pipelines you built from zero for hard roles, not just inbound you processed. Experience hiring engineers, plus comfort with commercial roles like AEs, partner managers or consultants. Experience hiring across European markets. Technically literate. You can read a GitHub profile, understand a stack and hold a credible first conversation with an engineer. You don't need to code, but you can't be bluffing in that call. A bar-raiser. You'll make the pass or fail call and stand behind it. Organised to a fault. A clean pipeline and an empty to-do list matter to you. You say it straight, to candidates, to hiring managers and to us. You already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and want to push that further. Nice to have German or another European language. Hiring in AI or B2B SaaS. You've built recruiting automations yourself (Ashby automations, Zapier, agents, anything). What we offer Competitive salary Seed-stage company backed by Index Ventures ($15M seed), led by our founder and CEO Tom Cupr, who previously founded one of Europe's largest online grocery retailers. Real ownership of your markets, and a say in how the talent function is built. Remote-first across Europe, with quarterly offsites in Prague. How we hire 30-min screen Working session: we give you a live Duvo role. You come back with the people you'd approach, the message you'd send, and your pass or fail calls on a set of real CVs, then walk us through it Final conversations with our founders We aim to close the loop in under 3 weeks. We're a small team building something hard. If that sounds like the right kind of problem, we'd like to talk. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Expect regular travel and periods of working on site with customers for several days in a week. title: AI Builder — Working Student
description: EggAI Labs · Working Student · In Person (Tübingen, Germany) Designing lifecycle evaluation for nondeterministic domain-specific AI systems. EggAI Labs We're opening the EggAI Labs in Tübingen. The Labs purpose is to test new AI capabilities, identify what works, how they'd improve delivery, and then build assets to support teams and clients. EggAI's mission cannot be achieved through one-off client projects alone and the Labs is the way to adapt and scale. As part of the first cohort, you will join a small peer group and work directly with EggAI's CAIO, a Tübingen alumnus. You will also collaborate with our engineering, product, and project leads, who will bring you insights from client problems, help you understand their context and challenge your solutions for them. Your fellow AI Builders will be deliberately chosen to span different passions and strenghts. You will have room to explore and be expected to turn that exploration into something useful. This is not a client-facing role. The problem: EvalOps How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions? We will explore EvalOps : the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way. These questions will guide the initial work: Regression suites : How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales? Coverage estimation : How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors? Live monitoring : Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals? Eval analysis : How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions. The role As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice: Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype. Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work. Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence. Communicate decisions and learning clearly. Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve. Code and build end to end. This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars. Three pillars, different passions Pillar Driving question Possible EvalOps focus Product What should we build? Workflows and interfaces that help domain experts create evals, inspect traces, understand results, and make decisions. Engineering How should we build it? Dependable and scalable evaluation infrastructure, trace processing, monitoring, and governance tooling. Data Science How do we know it works? Coverage measures, sampling strategies, scoring methods, statistical tests, anomaly detection, and reasoning under uncertainty. We expect every AI Builder to develop a practical foundation across all three pillars and to pursue greater depth in the one that most strongly matches their passion. What we value Problem obsession . A difficult question captures your curiosity. You keep returning to it, pursue ideas without waiting for instructions, and care deeply about finding an answer that works. Initiative and follow-through . You turn uncertainty into something you can investigate, test, and improve—and stay resourceful when the first approach fails. Evidence of making things work . Show us something you created, the decisions you made, and what you learned along the way. Independent judgment . You test new capabilities yourself, distinguish evidence from enthusiasm, and change your mind when the findings warrant it. Generosity in collaboration . You explain your thinking, seek candid feedback, act on it, and help others make progress. What is required You are pursuing a Master’s degree. You can write code and turn an idea into working, tested software. You can work from Tübingen and communicate fluently in English, our company language. Relevant fields include Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Bioinformatics, Computational Neuroscience, Medical Informatics, Quantitative Data Science, Cognitive Science. We also welcome candidates from other disciplines who can demonstrate strong problem-solving and practical technical ability. What you will gain Industry insight . Learn what works and what breaks in real enterprise AI systems, with access to problems from EggAI’s client work Meaningful ownership . Take an EvalOps problem from investigation to a working, evaluated solution, with freedom to shape the approach. Close mentorship . Work directly with EggAI’s Chief AI Officer and sharpen your judgment through feedback from engineering, product, and project leads. Room to develop . Deepen your strengths, learn from peers with complementary perspectives, and use modern AI-development tools on unresolved problems. A say in the Lab’s direction . Help establish its working practices, propose new questions, and influence what it pursues next. Competitive compensation , including recognition for exceptional contributions, and a potential path to a full-time EggAI role after graduation. How to apply A short cover letter is required. Your CV tells us what you have done so far, but we're also interested in the why . Use the letter to explain why you made those choices, what drives you, and why the AI Builder role at EggAI Labs feels like the right next step in your career. We are looking for exceptional students, and excellence takes many forms, e.g., academic results, research or ambitious projects. Whatever form yours takes, show us the appropriate evidence, be it grades, publications, something you've built or other evidence of impact. This is an in-person role in Tübingen. We can only consider candidates who live within commuting distance. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: Das Team von Elbphilharmonie und Laeiszhalle sucht zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt einen Haus- und Veranstaltungstechniker (m/w/div.) in der Laeiszhalle in Vollzeit. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 6 Monate befristet. Eine Verlängerung sowie eine spätere Übernahme in ein unbefristetes Beschäftigungsverhältnis können sich gegebenenfalls anschließen. Zu deinen Aufgaben gehört unter anderem: Wartung, Pflege und Instandhaltung der Veranstaltungs- und Gebäudetechnik Übernahme allgemeiner haustechnischer Tätigkeiten Auf- und Abbau von Bühnenmobiliar Steuerung der veranstaltungstechnischen Abläufe als technischer Inspizient Übernahme von Aufgaben und Pflichten als Verantwortlicher für Veranstaltungstechnik gemäß §§ 38, 40 Hmbg. VStättVO Bedienung der Veranstaltungstechnik entsprechend deiner Qualifikation und Erfahrung Unterstützung bei der Implementierung neuer Gebäude- und Veranstaltungstechnik im Rahmen der laufenden Sanierung sowie Begleitung von Inbetriebnahmen und Erstkonfigurationen Als fachliches Profil erwarten wir von dir: Abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung als Fachkraft für Veranstaltungstechnik oder eine abgeschlossene handwerkliche Berufsausbildung (z. B. Elektroniker, Gebäudetechniker) Fachrichtungsübergreifende Grundlagen in Licht-, Ton-, Video- und Netzwerktechnik Gute EDV-Grundkenntnisse (z. B. MS Office, CAD-Programme) Kenntnisse im Bereich Gebäudetechnik wünschenswert Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Deine persönlichen Voraussetzungen sind: Flexibilität bei der Arbeit im Rahmen von Sanierungsmaßnahmen Bereitschaft zur Tätigkeit in einem gemischten Haus- und Veranstaltungstechnikteam Begeisterung für technische Anlagen sowie Konzertveranstaltungen aller Art Hohes Maß an Organisations-, Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeit sowie Belastbarkeit Fähigkeit zum abteilungs- und gewerkübergreifenden Denken Sorgfältige und selbstständige Arbeitsweise Bereitschaft zur Arbeit an Wochenenden, Feiertagen und in den Abendstunden Über uns: Die Elbphilharmonie und Laeiszhalle Betriebsgesellschaft mbH ist die Betreiberin der Elbphilharmonie sowie der über 100 Jahre alten Laeiszhalle. In beiden Häusern finden neben den hauseigenen »Elbphilharmonie Konzerten« auch Konzerte externer Konzertveranstalter statt, zusammen etwa 1.000 Veranstaltungen pro Jahr. Die Abteilung Technik ist dem Unternehmensziel der umfassenden serviceorientierten Dienstleistung verpflichtet. Als erster Anlaufpunkt in den Bereichen Veranstaltungs- und Hausbetriebstechnik ist sie in der Lage einen umfassenden Veranstaltungsservice auf dem neusten Stand der Technik anzubieten. Arbeitsort: Dein Arbeitsort ist überwiegend die Laeiszhalle. Die Arbeitswege sind leider nicht durchgehend rollstuhlgerecht und daher für Menschen mit Mobilitätseinschränkungen nur eingeschränkt oder gar nicht zu bewältigen. Die Arbeitsplätze sind nicht rollstuhlgerecht ausgestattet. Gerne informieren wir dich über die vorhandenen Barrieren. Wir bieten: Spannende Tätigkeit in einem modernen Konzertbetrieb Kollegiale Atmosphäre in einem dynamischen Team Vergütung nach dem Tarifvertrag der Arbeitsrechtlichen Vereinigung Hamburg e. V. (AVH) in Entgeltgruppe 6, mit Einstufung nach individueller Vorerfahrung Attraktive Jahressonderzahlung Betriebliche Altersvorsorge nach dem Hamburger Zusatzversorgungsgesetz sowie Arbeitgeberzuschuss zu einem privaten Altersvorsorge-Modell Vergünstigungen bei Konzertkarten und Artikeln im Shop auf der Elbphilharmonie-Plaza Deutschland-Ticket des HVV inkl. Arbeitgeberzuschuss und gute Anbindung an den ÖPNV Dienstrad-Leasing 6 Wochen Urlaub pro Kalenderjahr Cafeteria mit Ausblick auf den Hamburger Hafen Events für Mitarbeitende Die Elbphilharmonie und Laeiszhalle Betriebsgesellschaft mbH verfolgt offensiv das Ziel der beruflichen Gleichstellung von Frauen und Männern und der Diversität. Wir sind bestrebt, die Vielfalt unserer Gesellschaft in unserer Organisation abzubilden und arbeiten an einem diskriminierungssensiblen Arbeitsumfeld. Wir glauben an die Stärke divers aufgestellter Teams und freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Personen, die uns durch andere Perspektiven und Erfahrungshorizonte ergänzen. Bewerbungen von BIPoC und Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund sind eindeutig erwünscht. In dem Bereich, für den diese Stelle ausgeschrieben wird, sind Frauen im Sinne des Hamburgischen Gleichstellungsgesetzes unterrepräsentiert. Bewerbungen von Frauen werden daher ausdrücklich begrüßt. Sie werden bei gleicher Eignung, Befähigung und fachlicher Leistung vorrangig berücksichtigt. Bewerbungen schwerbehinderter beziehungsweise gleichgestellter Menschen im Sinne des SGB IX sind eindeutig erwünscht. Sie werden bei gleicher Eignung besonders berücksichtigt. Wir haben dein Interesse geweckt? Dann bewirb dich jetzt mit aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (Anschreiben, Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse) ausschließlich über unser Online-Bewerbungsformular. title: Knit - Research Director
description: Knit is the AI-native consumer research platform helping brands automate and accelerate primary research. With our Researcher-Driven AI, we’ve condensed the entire quant + qual research process from weeks into days (sometimes hours!) for 50+ enterprise brands — including Amazon, T-Mobile, Mars, NASCAR, and more. We’re on a mission to scale and democratize world-class research. From survey generation to stakeholder-ready reports, our platform is redefining how insights teams operate — and we need your help to push the limits of what’s possible. Overview The purpose of the Research Director role is to ensure Knit customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their partnerships with Knit. By owning customer relationships, getting deeply engrained in customer research needs, and driving high-quality project deliverables, the Research Director’s impact is ultimately measured by positive customer retention and expansion. Responsibilities | What you will own... The research function is a primary contributor to Knit’s shared business objectives of customer retention and upsells, ultimately measured by Net Revenue Retention (NRR) in addition to supporting successful Pilot to Subscription Conversions for acquiring new business. The levers the Research Director role owns to influence these key business objectives are: Research Success → Ensuring Knit Customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their projects with Knit, measured by successfully achieving Research Objectives and delivering on Knit’s Quality & Speed service-level agreements (SLA’s) Primary responsibilities of this role: Serving as the dedicated research lead for all customers’ projects (on assigned accounts) and serving as the ultimate accountable party for research project success Driving and documenting in-depth project scoping to uncover a deep understanding of research objectives and project context to set up project success Driving as the strategic problem solver and research subject matter expert partner for customers, effectively being able to propose solutions to business & research needs Driving as a solutions architect for customers, educating them on Knit’s research capabilities, consulting with them to adjust for fringe requirements, and proposing solutions to maximize project success Driving, maintaining, and enriching all customer context to improve Knit’s ability to meet the customers’ custom research needs Participating in continuous innovation on Knit’s AI product to minimize the delta between Knit’s AI output and a human researcher output Being the final, customer-ready check and approver on all Knit final topline delivery and presenting the key insights and recommendations directly to the customers Driving on feedback collection on “the last mile” - uncovering and documenting what happens after Knit delivers a project to when it’s “stakeholder ready,” supporting Knit’s product vision in getting to stakeholder ready reports Successful & effective people management of direct reports, ensuring they are successfully fulfilling their role’s responsibilities and growing in impact (People Management at Knit includes driving performance, driving clarity and accountability, hiring, onboarding, upskilling competencies, performance management, conflict resolution, and morale building.) Required Skills & Experiences Required: Must have 8+ years of market research experience, with the majority of the time spent on the supplier side in a market research agency environment. Must have experience leading discovery and scoping calls, writing and editing quant and qual questionnaires from scratch, drafting analysis plans, and creating and presenting stakeholder-ready insights topline & reports. Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes in ambiguous environments, both for navigating complex customer needs and Knit internal business changes. Proven track record successfully operating in an early stage startup ( < 50 employees) is a plus. Proven track record of owning client relationships with customers at Enterprise, Fortune 500 US-based companies, specifically working with insights professionals to scope and achieve desired research outcomes, resulting in customer retention and growth. Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes successfully in environments with competing priorities, multiple research projects on at a given time, and simultaneous internal business demands. Effective People Manager both cross-functionally and at the team level - specifically in driving clarity and accountability, hiring, onboarding, performance management, conflict resolution, and morale building. Benefits Upon joining the Knit team, you will receive a competitive salary + commission plan if applicable to role, Equity Options, Healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), and Additional Coverage, a company laptop and one-time, onboarding Technology Stipend, a 401(k) with company match, flexible time-off, hybrid working, and more! Salary In accordance with New York pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role is $140,000 - $160,000. Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s level, experience, and qualifications upon joining Knit. Our Company Values We are the Championship Team. This means we: Are 1% better every day: We approach situations with a growth mindset and ask, “How can we make the business better?” and “What would it take?” Play to win: We set audacious goals and push ourselves to achieve them with a bias towards action (When we see a need, we take initiative, and hold ourselves accountable to seeing it through). Keep the main thing the main thing: Identify what has the biggest impact and prioritize to focus on it.
